Grounds in India

India grounds only, because the IPL teams play here. The files gave every match a venue number, not a stadium name, so each number was matched to a real stadium: take one match from the data, find that same match in a published scorecard, and the stadium in the scorecard is what the number means. For example, venue 1 is MA Chidambaram Stadium (Chepauk), Chennai, matched from Chennai Super Kings vs Lucknow Super Giants, IPL, 3 Apr 2023. Venue 3 is Wankhede Stadium, Mumbai, matched from Chennai Super Kings vs Kolkata Knight Riders, IPL, 26 Mar 2022. Venue 2 is M. Chinnaswamy Stadium, Bengaluru, matched from Royal Challengers Bengaluru vs Mumbai Indians, IPL, 2 Apr 2023. All 25 India grounds were matched this way, one by one. Open any player profile to see his full ground-by-ground record: where he played most, where his average is highest, and where he scored most. Foreign players show their single best ground in India.

Tap any ground in this table to open its own page: best batter, best bowler and the top 5 tables for that ground alone.

Rajasthan Royals home grounds in this data: Sawai Mansingh Stadium, Jaipur, and Barsapara Cricket Stadium, Guwahati, where Rajasthan Royals played home matches in IPL 2023. Mumbai has two separate grounds in the data, Wankhede Stadium and Brabourne Stadium, and Punjab has two, Mohali and Mullanpur, so a player's Mumbai or Punjab numbers are split by ground, not by city.

Tournaments

About the estimates. Only the Rajasthan Royals section has estimates, and every one is marked Estimate. An estimate is not a fact and not a promised auction price: it is a range worked out from the player’s stats in this dashboard’s data (runs, average, strike rate, wickets, economy and pressure numbers) and the verified 2025 auction prices of comparable players in the same role. The basis is printed next to every estimate so you can judge it yourself. One player, Kunal Singh Rathore, has no estimate: he has only 1 match in the data, which is too little to estimate from.

Sources and notes

    Batter & bowler splits

    The same ball-by-ball data cut new ways, for all 888 batters and 647 bowlers. Pick a batter or a bowler, then filter by phase, bowler type, pitch type and low or high scoring to see the numbers. Every player profile carries these same splits in full. Splits are one cut at a time: the file gives runs by phase, by bowler type and by match total separately, not combined, so each filter you set is shown as its own line.

    Batter splits cover 888 batters. Bowler splits cover 647 bowlers. Tap a name to load his splits below.

    Pitch types: the 30 classified venues

    Each venue with 10+ matches was classified from the data: average innings total (proxy, as above) and spinners share of bowler-credited wickets at that venue. Stadium names are shown only for the 25 Indian venues verified in venue_mapping.md; other venues show venue_name null and the country from matches.csv, so they are listed here by country and venue number. Spinner share is spinners’ share of bowler-credited wickets at the venue.

    Pitch type

    Definitions, exactly as computed

    • Phase: powerplay = overs 1-6, middle = overs 7-15, death = overs 16-20 PLUS super overs (innings 3-4). NOTE: this differs slightly from players.json, where phase is by over number only and super-over balls fall in powerplay; here death includes super overs, so a batter phase-death equals players.json pressure.
    • Balls: Deliveries except wides. Legal balls bowled exclude wides and no-balls. Bowler runs conceded = bat runs + 1 per wide + 1 per no-ball.
    • International bowler: the bowler played (is_played=true in playing_eleven.csv) at least one T20I-format match in the dataset (competition match_format = T20I).
    • Established / known good bowler: 50 or more bowler-credited wickets in the dataset.
    • Uncapped bowler: NOT a dataset-T20I player AND has a web_player_data.json entry whose career ODI and T20I are both null. Players with no web entry and no dataset T20I are “unknown” (count in uncapped_unknown) and are NOT counted as uncapped. The dataset itself contains no ODI matches, so the dataset half of the rule is the T20I check only.
    • All-rounder: 300+ runs AND 15+ wickets in the dataset (players.json). Split by contribution scores: bat_score = (runs per match)/20, bowl_score = (wickets per match)/1.0; bat_score > bowl_score = batting all-rounder (bat_ar), otherwise bowling all-rounder (bowl_ar).
    • Bowler types are NOT exclusive buckets. A bowler can be international AND established AND an all-rounder; the batter runs vs each type are recorded separately.
    • Vs bowler / vs team: Per batter, runs/balls/outs vs each bowler faced, top 10 by balls faced. Batting: runs/balls vs each opposition (bowling) team. Bowling: wickets/runs/balls vs each opposition (batting) team.
    • Clutch, won chase: Batting in innings 2 of a match where the batting team won (win_team_id = batting team). Runs/balls/outs/SR/avg and innings count.
    • Clutch, last 2 overs of a won chase: Runs/balls in overs 19-20 of innings 2 in a won chase (only balls that exist; a chase won earlier has no overs 19-20).
    • Clutch, won vs lost matches: Runs/balls/outs in matches the batters team won vs lost (team from playing_eleven for that match; win_team_id from matches.csv). 41 matches have no win_team_id and are excluded from both.
    • Not-out finishes: Times the batter batted in innings 2 of a won chase and was not dismissed in that innings (i.e. was at the crease when the chase was won).
    • Innings total proxy: Innings total = sum of bat runs in the innings + 1 per wide + 1 per no-ball. Leg-byes and byes are NOT recoverable from the data (the extras columns are type codes, not run counts), so the proxy UNDERCOUNTS the true total by the leg-byes/byes in that innings (typically a few runs).
    • Low-scoring: Innings where the batting teams proxy total was <= 140. High-scoring: Innings where the batting teams proxy total was >= 180.
    • Pitch types, method: Each venue with 10+ matches was classified from the data: average innings total (proxy, as above) and spinners share of bowler-credited wickets at that venue.
    • Spin pitch: spinners took >= 44% of bowler-credited wickets at the venue (overall spinner share is 36.7%). Batting pitch: average innings total (proxy) >= 175, and not a spin pitch. Bowling pitch: average innings total (proxy) <= 150, and not a spin pitch. Balanced: Any other venue with 10+ matches.
    • Unclassified venues: Venues with fewer than 10 matches (67 venues, 238 matches) are not classified; balls bowled at those venues are excluded from the per-bowler pitch splits.
    • Dismissed batter’s role: On each bowler-credited wicket, the dismissed batters role is: batting all-rounder / bowling all-rounder if he meets the all-rounder rule above (checked first); otherwise by his batting position in that match: 1-3 top-order, 4-7 middle-order, 8+ tail-ender.
    • Bowler credit: Bowler is credited the wicket for every dismissal except Run Out, Retire Out and Obstructing the field (both spellings Obstracting/Obstructing normalised). Dismissal types normalised: Stump -> Stumped, RunOut -> Run Out.
    • Averages: Batting average = runs / dismissals (null if never dismissed in that split). Strike rate = 100*runs/balls (null if 0 balls). Economy = 6*runs/balls. Bowling average = runs/wickets (null if 0 wickets).
    • Counts: 888 batters, 647 bowlers, 30 venues with 10+ matches, 719 T20I players in the dataset, 61 established bowlers (50+ wickets), 175 uncapped bowlers, 32 uncapped unknown, 40 all-rounders (20 batting all-rounders, 20 bowling all-rounders). Only splits with actual data are included per player (no zero-filled rows). Toss splits were mentioned by the user in conversation but are not in this task spec, so no toss splits were computed.

    How the numbers are made

    • Balls faced exclude wides. Legal balls bowled exclude wides and no-balls.
    • Bowler runs conceded = batsman runs + 1 per wide + 1 per no-ball. Leg-byes and byes are not charged to the bowler.
    • The extras columns in the raw file are type codes, not run counts, so team totals cannot be rebuilt from them.
    • Dismissed player is counted out. Run outs can be the non-striker. Bowlers are credited the wicket for every dismissal except Run Out, Retire Out and Obstructing the field.
    • Pressure = death overs (16 to 20) plus super overs (innings 3 and 4). Chase pressure is the second-innings death-overs subset, shown separately in each profile.
    • Matches played come from the playing XI file. Innings = match-innings in which the player batted or bowled.
    • 16 of 883 matches have no ball-by-ball rows, so the analysis covers 867 matches and 200,999 deliveries.
    • Phases: powerplay is overs 1 to 6, middle is overs 7 to 15, death is overs 16 to 20.
    • Grounds: stadium names come from the verified venue matching described in the Grounds in India section. Matches at a ground come from the playing-XI file, and batting and bowling at a ground use the same ball rules as the rest of the dashboard.
    • Highest average ground needs at least 30 balls faced at that ground, so one big innings cannot decide it. The Balls column sits next to every average in the grounds table.
    • IPL teams come from the competition team mapping file, season by season, with team names exactly as written there, for example Rajasthan Royals. A player counts as Indian if he played T20I for India or is on the Indian player list in the data. Everyone else is shown as a foreign player, with his single best ground in India only.
    • Tournaments: only competitions present in the files are shown, 138 in total. There is no T20 World Cup or Champions League data in the files, so neither is shown.
    • Career beyond this dataset: the local and domestic teams, ODI, T20I, first-class (Ranji Trophy level), List A and IPL figures inside each player profile come from the web, not from the files: Cricbuzz player profiles for ODI, T20I and IPL, and Wikipedia career tables for first-class and List A, accessed on 2026-11-10. Each profile links its source. A dash means the player has not played that format, or the source gives no figure for it. The first-class and List A sources give no strike rate or economy, so those cells are always a dash. The IPL row is the player's IPL career from Cricbuzz, not all T20 cricket. Ranji Trophy is played for the state team, for example Mumbai, not for the IPL team.
    • Best of the day: for each of the 686 match dates, the top 3 batters and top 3 bowlers use only that day's balls in the document, never the whole dataset. Best batter is the most runs that day (tie: higher strike rate); best bowler is the most wickets that day (tie: lower economy). Man of the match is the document's own value, resolved from its player number to a name, and shown as a dash where the document has none: 764 of 883 matches have one. A few dates have matches but no ball-by-ball rows, so no best batter or bowler can be worked out for those dates.
    • IPL Salaries & Auction Value: prices are IPL 2025 season salaries from published sources (Wikipedia 2025 personnel changes, SportzBuzz auction list, Indian Express RR squad list, Cricbuzz auction tracker and IPL.com for the 2026 Rajasthan Royals list), listed in full on the Salaries page. The auction value ranges for Rajasthan Royals players are estimates only, never facts: each is anchored on the player’s stats in this dashboard’s dataset and the verified 2025 prices of comparable players named in its basis. Two 2026 trade prices are not confirmed and are shown as such on the Salaries page: Ravindra Jadeja’s trade price is listed as ₹14 cr by IPL.com and ₹18 cr by some other outlets, and the 2026 prices for Sam Curran and Donovan Ferreira were not separately published.
    • Best of the stadium: for each of the 25 India stadiums, the top 5 batters by runs, the top 5 batters by average (minimum 30 balls faced at that ground), the top 5 bowlers by wickets and the top 5 bowlers by economy (minimum 24 balls bowled at that ground) use only the balls bowled at that ground, with matches at the ground counted from the playing-XI file. Averages sit next to the balls and matches behind them, so small samples stay visible.
    • Batter and bowler splits (Splits page and every player profile): computed for ALL batters in the dataset: 888 batters and 647 bowlers (same counts as players.json). The user said "256 batters" but no 256 count exists in the data.
    • Splits phase: powerplay = overs 1-6, middle = overs 7-15, death = overs 16-20 PLUS super overs (innings 3-4). NOTE: this differs slightly from players.json, where phase is by over number only and super-over balls fall in powerplay; here death includes super overs, so a batter phase-death equals players.json pressure.
    • Splits bowler types: International bowler: the bowler played (is_played=true in playing_eleven.csv) at least one T20I-format match in the dataset (competition match_format = T20I). Established / known good bowler: 50 or more bowler-credited wickets in the dataset. Uncapped bowler: NOT a dataset-T20I player AND has a web_player_data.json entry whose career ODI and T20I are both null. Players with no web entry and no dataset T20I are "unknown" (count in uncapped_unknown) and are NOT counted as uncapped. The dataset itself contains no ODI matches, so the dataset half of the rule is the T20I check only. All-rounder: 300+ runs AND 15+ wickets in the dataset (players.json). Split by contribution scores: bat_score = (runs per match)/20, bowl_score = (wickets per match)/1.0; bat_score > bowl_score = batting all-rounder (bat_ar), otherwise bowling all-rounder (bowl_ar). Bowler types are NOT exclusive buckets. A bowler can be international AND established AND an all-rounder; the batter runs vs each type are recorded separately.
    • Splits vs bowler and vs team: Per batter, runs/balls/outs vs each bowler faced, top 10 by balls faced. Batting: runs/balls vs each opposition (bowling) team. Bowling: wickets/runs/balls vs each opposition (batting) team.
    • Splits clutch: won_chase: Batting in innings 2 of a match where the batting team won (win_team_id = batting team). Runs/balls/outs/SR/avg and innings count. won_chase_last2: Runs/balls in overs 19-20 of innings 2 in a won chase (only balls that exist; a chase won earlier has no overs 19-20). won_matches / lost_matches: Runs/balls/outs in matches the batters team won vs lost (team from playing_eleven for that match; win_team_id from matches.csv). 41 matches have no win_team_id and are excluded from both. not_out_finishes: Times the batter batted in innings 2 of a won chase and was not dismissed in that innings (i.e. was at the crease when the chase was won).
    • Splits low and high scoring: Innings total = sum of bat runs in the innings + 1 per wide + 1 per no-ball. Leg-byes and byes are NOT recoverable from the data (the extras columns are type codes, not run counts), so the proxy UNDERCOUNTS the true total by the leg-byes/byes in that innings (typically a few runs). Low: Innings where the batting teams proxy total was <= 140. High: Innings where the batting teams proxy total was >= 180.
    • Splits pitch types: Each venue with 10+ matches was classified from the data: average innings total (proxy, as above) and spinners share of bowler-credited wickets at that venue. Spin pitch: spinners took >= 44% of bowler-credited wickets at the venue (overall spinner share is 36.7%). Batting pitch: average innings total (proxy) >= 175, and not a spin pitch. Bowling pitch: average innings total (proxy) <= 150, and not a spin pitch. Balanced: Any other venue with 10+ matches. Unclassified: Venues with fewer than 10 matches (67 venues, 238 matches) are not classified; balls bowled at those venues are excluded from the per-bowler pitch splits. Venue names: Stadium names only for the 25 Indian venues verified in venue_mapping.md; other venues show venue_name null and the country from matches.csv. Counts: 30 venues with 10+ matches (12 balanced, 8 batting, 5 spin, 5 bowling).
    • Splits dismissed batter role: On each bowler-credited wicket, the dismissed batters role is: batting all-rounder / bowling all-rounder if he meets the all-rounder rule above (checked first); otherwise by his batting position in that match: 1-3 top-order, 4-7 middle-order, 8+ tail-ender. Batting position source: playing_eleven.csv batting_order for that match and player; if missing, the batting_order on the ball row where he was striker; if neither exists, role = unknown.
    • Splits bowler credit and averages: Bowler is credited the wicket for every dismissal except Run Out, Retire Out and Obstructing the field (both spellings Obstracting/Obstructing normalised). Dismissal types normalised: Stump -> Stumped, RunOut -> Run Out. Batting average = runs / dismissals (null if never dismissed in that split). Strike rate = 100*runs/balls (null if 0 balls). Economy = 6*runs/balls. Bowling average = runs/wickets (null if 0 wickets). Only splits with actual data are included per player (no zero-filled rows).
    • Splits not computed: Toss splits were mentioned by the user in conversation but are not in this task spec, so no toss splits were computed. Per-batter runs vs bowler type for bowlers whose uncapped status is unknown are not counted under uncapped (see uncapped_unknown count). 16 of 883 matches have no ball-by-ball rows and contribute nothing to any split.
    Dataset: IPL and T20I, 22 Jan 2022 to 1 Nov 2026. 867 matches with ball-by-ball data, 200,999 deliveries, 141 competitions, 958 players with stats (888 batters, 647 bowlers). Total runs off the bat: 269,550. Bowler-credited wickets: 10,272. Total dismissals: 10,878. Leaderboard, grounds and tournament numbers are computed directly from the ball-by-ball file. Nothing is estimated. Career beyond this dataset figures in player profiles come from the web and were accessed on 2026-11-10. Grounds cover the 25 India stadiums for the 445 players who played in India. Tournament tables cover all 138 competitions in the files. Splits cover all 888 batters and 647 bowlers, with pitch types for the 30 venues with 10 or more matches.
